english.title: Employee fail to discharge general health and safety duty at work

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: Health and safety at Work etc Act 1974

english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being an employee of **(..SPECIFY EMPLOYER..), failed, while at work to

(A)_[take reasonable care for the health and safety of yourself and of other persons who may have been affected by your acts and omissions at work]_
(B)_[co-operate with your employer so far as was necessary to enable a duty or requirement imposed by or under a relevant statutory provision, namely **(..SPECIFY DUTY OR REQUIREMENT AND STATUTORY PROVISION..), to be performed or complied with]_
(C)_[co-operate with **(..SPECIFY PERSON..) so far as was necessary to enable a duty or requirement imposed by or under a relevant statutory provision, namely **(..SPECIFY DUTY OR REQUIREMENT AND STATUTORY PROVISION..), to be performed or complied with]_
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 7 and 33(1)(a) of, and Schedule 3A to, of the Health and Safety at Work etc Act 1974.

english.notes: Proceedings for an offence shall not, in England and Wales, be instituted except by an inspector or the Environment Agency or by or with the consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions, see section 38 of the Health and Safety at Work etc Act 1974.

consent.description: Health and Safety at Work Inspectorate

other.penalty:
Either way -
Summary: 6/12 months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: 2 years imprisonment and / or a fine.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2002; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see Schedule 3A to the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2020.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
